transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from organizing spools of thread behind the counter*

Good afternoon, sir! Welcome to Mr. Henderson's Fine Tailoring. I'm afraid Mr. Henderson himself has traveled to Philadelphia on business and won't return for another three weeks at least. 

*notices the garment bag in your hands*

Is that one of our pieces? How may I be of service today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, it arrived today and it is quite unsatisfactory.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up and peers at the garment with a practiced eye*

Unsatisfactory, you say? Well now, that's quite unfortunate to hear, sir. Mr. Henderson takes great pride in his work.

*reaches for the shop ledger*

May I have your name for our records? And what specifically seems to be the trouble with the garment? Perhaps it's something simple that just needs a bit of adjustment...

*trails off while flipping through pages of orders*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, yes. A Mr. Abraham Lincoln. It appears that you've made a recent order for a suit, quite a fancy one too.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*runs finger down the ledger page and stops*

Ah yes, here we are—Mr. Abraham Lincoln. A black frock coat and trousers, finest wool. Custom measurements taken by Mr. Henderson himself just over a month ago.

*looks up with a polite but somewhat guarded expression*

Now then, Mr. Lincoln, what exactly is unsatisfactory about the suit? Mr. Henderson was quite particular about those measurements. Did you try the full ensemble on properly?

*crosses arms and leans slightly against the counter*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Well, it seems there may have been a miscalculation in the measurements. The sleeves are quite short, and the overall fit is quite loose. Additionally, the fabric used for the coat is a cheaper weave than what was agreed upon.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*frowns and pulls the garment closer to examine it, running fingers over the fabric*

A cheaper weave? Sir, I assure you Mr. Henderson uses only the materials specified in the order. This is the wool that was requested—

*pauses and looks back at the ledger, then up at you with a firmer expression*

Now, as for the fit, Mr. Lincoln, I must remind you that all custom orders are final upon pickup. The receipt you signed when collecting the garment states quite clearly that no alterations or refunds are given once the piece leaves the shop. 

*taps the ledger with one finger*

Mr. Henderson took your measurements himself, and I'm certain they were accurate. Perhaps you've... well, grown accustomed to a different style of fit? Some gentlemen prefer their coats looser than what's currently fashionable.

*meets your eyes directly*

I'm afraid with Mr. Henderson away for weeks, and with our shop policy being what it is, there's precious little I can do for you today, sir.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: This isn't about the money. If I had paid the same amount for a pair of trousers I could wear anywhere in the country, I would expect them to fit correctly the first time. I am not willing to accept subpar tailoring, regardless of the price.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stiffens slightly, a hint of defensiveness creeping into my voice*

Mr. Lincoln, with all due respect, Mr. Henderson has been tailoring in this city for over twenty years. His reputation is impeccable. Subpar tailoring is simply not something that leaves this shop.

*gestures at the garment*

You signed the receipt acknowledging the terms. Custom work is precisely that—custom. Once you walked out that door with the suit, the transaction was complete. I cannot authorize refunds or alterations without Mr. Henderson present, and certainly not when our policy explicitly forbids it.

*softens tone slightly but remains firm*

Perhaps when Mr. Henderson returns in three weeks' time, you could speak with him directly about your concerns. But I must be honest with you, sir—he stands by his work, and he stands by the terms every customer agrees to. The measurements were taken with care, the materials were as ordered.

*looks at you squarely*

I understand your frustration, truly I do. But my hands are tied by shop policy and by Mr. Henderson's absence. Is there anything else I might help you with today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: No, I suppose there isn't. But again, thank you for your understanding.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods, expression softening just a touch at your gracious response*

I appreciate your civility in this matter, Mr. Lincoln. Many men would have raised quite a fuss.

*makes a note in the ledger*

I will make certain to inform Mr. Henderson of your visit and your concerns when he returns. He may wish to contact you himself, though I cannot promise what he'll say regarding the policy.

*steps back from the counter*

Good day to you, sir. I do hope the suit serves you well despite your reservations.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, sir. I'll take the suit. But if there comes a time when the design is no longer fashionable, I might consider selling it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*chuckles dryly and shakes head*

Well, Mr. Lincoln, a black frock coat of good wool never truly goes out of fashion in this city. It's a staple of any gentleman's wardrobe.

*waves hand dismissively but not unkindly*

Though I suppose if you find yourself tired of it, there's always someone looking for quality tailoring, even second-hand. Mr. Henderson's work tends to hold its value.

*returns to organizing the spools of thread*

Safe travels to you, sir. And do give that suit a fair chance—sometimes these things grow on a man after a few wearings.

Good afternoon, Mr. Lincoln.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Good afternoon, Miss. How may I assist you today?"

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up, slightly confused*

I beg your pardon, Mr. Lincoln? I'm afraid I don't follow. Were you addressing someone else?

*glances toward the door to see if another customer has entered the shop*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: No, I was simply greeting Miss with a polite farewell. She has just left the premises.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*blinks in confusion and looks around the shop*

Sir, I'm not sure what you mean. There's been no lady here—it's just been you and myself this entire conversation. 

*studies you with a mixture of concern and puzzlement*

Are you feeling quite well, Mr. Lincoln? Perhaps the afternoon heat has gotten to you? Would you like a glass of water before you take your leave?

*gestures toward a small chair near the window*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Oh, I apologize if I seemed out of sorts. I must admit, the heat has taken quite a toll on me. A glass of water would indeed be welcome. Thank you for your concern." *settles into the chair*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*relaxes slightly and nods*

Of course, sir. Just a moment.

*disappears through a curtained doorway to the back room and returns shortly with a tin cup of water*

Here you are, Mr. Lincoln. 

*hands you the cup*

It's drawn fresh from the well this morning, so it should still be cool. This August heat can addle anyone's senses, especially if you've been walking about the city in that heavy coat of yours.

*leans against the counter, watching you with a touch of concern*

Take your time, sir. No rush. The shop's quiet this afternoon anyway.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you, Miss. Your kindness is quite touching. I appreciate your concern for my well-being." *takes a sip of water* "As for the suit, I'm afraid I'm still not satisfied with the quality. The stitching is uneven, and the fabric seems of a lower grade than what was specified. I'm afraid I will need to take it back and have it repaired or exchanged."

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Lincoln shows rigid focus on the suit complaint despite clear policy, never exploring alternative perspectives or creative solutions when told 'my hands are tied.'

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He persists in demanding proper tailoring standards ('I would expect them to fit correctly the first time'), but then suddenly becomes confused and contradictory about his complaint.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Lincoln remains formal and reserved throughout ('Good afternoon, sir'), showing minimal warmth or engagement beyond the transactional complaint.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Initially polite ('thank you for your understanding') when dismissed, but then becomes oddly persistent and disconnected, calling the clerk 'Miss' repeatedly despite corrections.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Shows increasing disorientation and confusion, hallucinating a woman's presence, contradicting himself about accepting the suit, suggesting psychological distress or instability.
